title: Motion-Energy Conservation Choreographer
description: The user choreographs a dance routine between Xbot and a facial-capture head mounted on a ShadowmappableMesh pedestal. A conserved 'motion energy' pool is shared between both characters: boosting one animation's speed or intensity drains energy from the other. The user sequences animation clips, adjusts energy distribution, and uses undo/redo to refine the performance.
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 with GLTFLoader and OrbitControls from CDN. Load Xbot.glb on the left, facecap.glb attached atop ShadowmappableMesh.glb as a pedestal on the right. Use a PerspectiveCamera at (0,1.5,4) looking at origin. Add a DirectionalLight casting shadows onto a ground plane and onto ShadowmappableMesh. Enable shadow maps on the renderer.

Implement a conserved motion-energy system: a total pool of 100 energy units shared between Xbot body animations and facecap morph-target animations. Display an energy bar HUD at the top showing the split. Provide two vertical sliders (HTML range inputs) labeled 'Body Energy' and 'Face Energy' that are coupled so increasing one decreases the other, preserving the sum at 100. Body Energy scales Xbot AnimationMixer timeScale (0.1 to 2.0). Face Energy scales the morph target influence intensity and cycling speed on facecap (0.0 to 1.0 influence, 0.2x to 3.0x cycle speed).

Add a timeline sequencer at the bottom with 6 slots. The user clicks a slot then picks from available Xbot animation clips via a dropdown to assign that clip to the slot. A Play button plays slots sequentially, each for 3 seconds, blending energy distribution per slot. Each slot stores its own energy split. Clicking a filled slot allows reassigning or clearing it.

Implement full undo/redo (Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Shift+Z) tracking every state change: energy slider adjustments, clip assignments, and slot clears. Maintain a history stack of at least 30 states. Show undo/redo buttons in the UI with step counters.

Add a 'Mirror' toggle that swaps the energy values between body and face across all slots simultaneously (one undoable action). Add a 'Randomize' button that fills all empty slots with random clips and random energy splits while preserving the conservation law. The ShadowmappableMesh pedestal should glow (emissive intensity) proportional to Face Energy. Ensure smooth 60fps animation loop.
